title: Canonicalize metering checkpoints and align rate-window counters for hybrid streaming sessions
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Summary:
We are seeing small but persistent discrepancies between usage recorded by the streaming metering pipeline and the quota/rate-limit windows for hybrid sessions (sessions that begin as non-streaming requests and switch to streaming, or vice versa). These mismatches show up as: (a) short-lived quota exceedances without client-visible error, (b) apparent double credits when reconnect+resume occurs, and (c) drift between token totals in Analytics vs Billing (0.02% - 0.2% observed in production).

Background & problem statement:
- Root cause clusters observed: inconsistent checkpoint placement across the ingestion path, misaligned atomicity between the rate-window aggregator and the prefix/KV cache flush, and tokenization variance when clients send pre-tokenized counts in fragments.
- Edge cases triggering errors include reconnects during active rate-window boundary transitions, multipart uploads where final fragment triggers model switch, and hybrid API calls where an initial synchronous response upgraded to streaming.
- Current pipeline lacks a single canonical checkpoint that the quota service trusts; multiple best-effort checkpoints create race windows where the quota window and the metering aggregate diverge.

Proposed design (high level):
1) Introduce a lightweight "metering-checkpoint" envelope emitted at two coordinated places: ingress (after canonical server-side tokenization) and after the KV-cache flush (post-model-inference finalization). The envelope contains a stable session fingerprint and monotonic fragment index.
2) Implement a window-aligner microservice inside metering that: (a) converts checkpoint envelopes to idempotent ledger writes, (b) assigns tokens to discrete rate-windows using a deterministic boundary algorithm, and (c) emits compensating deltas on mismatch.
3) Server-side canonicalization: add an optional flag to force server-side tokenization and ignore client-submitted token counts for any session that may cross streaming boundaries. Trade-off: small CPU cost vs. correctness benefits.
4) Rollout strategy: feature-flag the canonical tokenization per-customer and route 5% of total realtime traffic through the window-aligner for 2 weeks. Monitor divergence metrics before widening.

Telemetry & success criteria:
- New metrics to add: metering.checkpoint_lag_ms, metering.window_mismatch_rate, metering.compensation_deltas_per_min, metering.idempotent_write_rejections.
- Goal: reduce Analytics vs Billing token drift to <0.01% over 24h for canary traffic and eliminate duplicate credits on reconnects for flagged sessions.
- Alerting: fire P1 if window_mismatch_rate > 0.1% for >10m on canary.

Implementation notes & decisions made so far:
- Chosen deterministic boundary algorithm: assign tokens to window by the timestamp of the first non-empty checkpoint that references that fragment index. This favours reproducibility across retries.
- Decided against always trusting client-provided token counts due to observed client-side tokenizer differences (varies across SDK versions). Instead, server-side canonicalization is opt-in via account flag; globally we will keep accepting client counts but the window-aligner will reconcile and emit compensations when discrepancies exceed threshold.
- To minimize write amplification, idempotent ledger writes use (session_fingerprint, fragment_index) as the unique key and store a compact checksum of the token vector.

Testing & validation plan:
- Extend the metering sim harness to create hybrid clients that flip between sync/stream modes mid-session, inject clock skew (±400ms), and simulate reconnects with overlapping fragments.
- Add fault-injection for late checkpoint deliveries and duplicated fragments to verify compensating delta logic.
- Run canary with internal customers for two weeks; compare daily aggregates between billing_export and analytics_export.

- Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/metering/pull/3789
- Simulation harness repo branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/meter-sim/tree/eng-205113-aligner
- Observability dashboard (canary): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd123/metering-checkpoints-canary

Next steps:
- (Marco) finish window-aligner PoC and unit tests (ETA: 2026-03-17).
- (Aisha) wire up new telemetry and add alert rules (ETA: 2026-03-12).
- (Priya K.) run extended sim harness for 48h and produce validation report (ETA: 2026-03-20).

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: CPU overhead from server-side tokenization may increase inference ingress latency. Mitigation: make server-side tokenization opt-in and benchmark in canary; measure p50/p95 latency delta and set account-level guardrails.
- Risk: idempotent ledger writes could create a new hot key pattern. Mitigation: shard ledger by session_fingerprint prefix and implement local cache of recent fragments.
comments: 2026-02-02 - Aisha Raman: Pulled initial production logs and traced two incidents where totals drifted by ~0.12%. Suspect race window between prefix cache flush and quota window close. Created PoC for checkpoint envelope.

2026-02-12 - Marco Liu: Implemented early version of idempotent write; unit tests for dedupe pass. Observed a case where client token counts differ because of normalization differences in whitespace handling. Added canonical tokenizer prototype to PoC.

2026-02-25 - Security review (notes): No new PII is stored in checkpoint payloads. Checkpoint contains only session_fingerprint, fragment_index, token_count_checksum. Recommend encryption-in-transit and enforce minimal retention (7 days) for ledger writes.

2026-03-01 - QA (Priya Kapoor): Sim harness run #7 with reconnect injection shows compensating deltas working; duplicate credits avoided in 98/100 trials. Two failing cases tied to out-of-order fragments >1s — need stronger monotonic fragment enforcement.

2026-03-05 - Product feedback (Liam O'Connor): For Dedicated customers with strict latency SLAs, prefer opt-out for server-side tokenization. We'll expose an account-level flag and a recommended guardrail in Console.
2026-03-09 - Marco Liu: Integrated window-aligner with quota service; canary deploy queued. Draft PR linked above. Preparing migration doc for rollbacks and compensating runs.
2026-03-10 - Aisha Raman: Added Grafana panel links and alert thresholds to ticket. Marked customer_impact high and set canary to 5% traffic initially.
